title: Unify client config schema and orchestrate dependency bump wave across Python/JS/Go SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Multiple SDKs expose slightly different client configuration keys (timeout vs request_timeout, model -> model_name, enable_streaming boolean diverges). This causes accidental regressions in multi-language integrations and complicates runtime routing and documentation. We need a coordinated wave to: (1) define and land a single canonical config schema with clear backwards-compat shims, (2) bump critical transitive deps (http clients, auth, serialization libraries) to address CVEs and performance regressions, and (3) remove deprecated surface that blocks consistent behavior across environments. The goal is to reduce support noise, improve test coverage for cross-language parity, and unblock future runtime features that rely on canonical config semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A single, documented canonical client config schema is accepted and published in the SDK RFC and repo READMEs
Python/JS/Go SDKs accept both new keys and deprecated aliases for one release with runtime warnings
All three SDKs have critical dependency upgrades applied and CI green on the canary branch
No customer-facing API behavior is changed without opt-in (feature flags or minor version bumps)
Migration guide and changelog entries are published; at least two internal reference apps tested
Rollout plan exists that sequences language bumps to minimize cross-team churn
tasks: Draft canonical config schema (owner: Miguel) and circulate for PM/Docs/Design review
Implement aliasing layer in Python SDK to map deprecated keys to canonical names and emit warnings
Apply equivalent aliasing implementation in JS and Go SDKs
Bump http/transport libraries: python-requests -> 2.31, node-fetch replacement check, go-http-client pin
Run cross-language parity integration tests against runtime-staging and collect diffs
Create migration guide + examples for common patterns (streaming, retry config, model pinning)
Coordinate release dates and draft deprecation schedule (one release with warnings, removal six weeks later)
Open compatibility PRs and request engineering reviews from SDK owners
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with SDK leads (Python: Li Chen, JS: Priya Nair, Go: Daniel Kim). Agreed on canonical key names and aliasing approach.
2026-02-28: Canonical schema v0.1 posted to docs repo: https://docs.internal.redwood/workflows/sdk-config-v0.1 (internal). Asked PM to confirm customer-impact matrix.
2026-03-03: Python alias layer prototype merged to feature branch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/412). Emits DeprecationWarning for deprecated keys.
2026-03-07: Dependency audit completed. Identified two high-priority CVEs in transitive JS package 'whatwg-url' (patched in latest node-fetch replacement).
2026-03-10: Integration test run against runtime-staging failed on streaming flag semantics between JS SDK and runtime; root cause: boolean coercion difference. Fix landed in JS SDK PR #87.
2026-03-12: Alignment doc updated with final keys and examples. Planning to open coordinated PRs for Go and JS tomorrow and schedule canary releases the week of 2026-03-16.
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/87 - normalize streaming flag coercion and bump transport deps
https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/129 - introduce canonical config enums and update client constructor
risks: Risk: aliasing layer may miss edge-case keys used by third-party customers -> mitigation: run telemetry scan for deprecated keys across last 90 days
Risk: dependency bumps could surface ABI differences in compiled Go tooling -> mitigation: run extended integration matrix on release branch
Risk: simultaneous releases across languages cause docs drift -> mitigation: freeze docs copy and release changelog snapshots
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive removal of deprecated keys reduces long-term maintenance but increases short-term support load. We chose a 2-step deprecation (warn then remove) to balance.
Follow-ups: schedule a customer communication for customers with heavy SDK usage and identify top 10 accounts using deprecated keys.
Next milestone: canary release of all three SDKs to internal alpha accounts by 2026-03-23
